text:
alex: Quick heads-up — I ran `terraform plan` in staging and it's proposing to recreate the ElastiCache replication_group (aws_elasticache_replication_group.redis) because the parameter_group_name drifted after someone tweaked maxmemory-policy in the console. Not comfortable recreating in place. Anyone seen this pattern? Want recommended approach: import, taint, or edit TF to match console? :eyes:

jin: Oof. Do you have the exact diff? Usually plan shows something like `parameter_group_name: "rg-default" => "rg-custom-2026-03"`. If it's just the param group name change, import the parameter group resource into state or update TF to reference the new group.

alex: Plan shows: `~ parameter_group_name (forces new resource) "redis-legacy" => "redis-legacy-mod"`. Also there is a `~` on replication_group that would replace the whole cluster (destroy/create). I didn't touch anything manually.

marta: If the console change is authoritative, best is to import the updated parameter group into Terraform (or create a TF resource that matches). Avoid taint if you want to preserve data. Steps I do:
1) `terraform import aws_elasticache_parameter_group.pg redis-legacy-mod`
2) `terraform refresh`
3) `terraform plan`

chris: If the parameter group was created out-of-band, importing is safest. If you can't import (name mismatch), you can attach `lifecycle ignore_changes` for `parameter_group_name` as a short-term workaround, but that's tech debt.

alex: Trying import now. Getting lock errors in the remote state (DynamoDB lock). `terraform init` succeeded but `terraform apply` blocked by lock ID 'abc123' for 20m.

terraform-bot: Automatic message: Remote state lock detected in DynamoDB (LockID: abc123). See ops-runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/terraform-locks

jin: If lock is stuck, check which CI job holds it:
```
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-state-locks --key '{"LockID": {"S": "abc123"}}'
```
then `Owner` field shows user/job. If it's stale, you can `aws dynamodb delete-item` but coordinate.

marta: Also try `terraform force-unlock abc123` (use the lock ID from `terraform plan` output). Prefer `force-unlock` to directly deleting the row.

alex: Owner shows `jenkins/44` but that job finished hours ago. I'll coordinate with SRE before nuking lock.

sre-team: Pinged Jenkins team — confirmed job failed due to worker OOM and left lock. Go ahead to force-unlock when ready. Recommend running `terraform force-unlock "abc123"` from your machine, then re-run `terraform import ...`.

alex: Did force-unlock, import ran but now `terraform plan` still wants to replace the replication_group because the parameter group association is computed on the replication_group resource. Any way to avoid full replacement?

chris: You can try:
1) create a TF resource for the parameter group with the new name, import it
2) update `parameter_group_name` on replication_group resource in TF to reference that resource
3) `terraform apply` should then do an in-place update if the provider supports it. But sometimes the provider forces replacement — check provider docs.

marta: Alternative: Use `aws cli` to attach the parameter group to the cluster manually (so the infra matches TF), then `terraform refresh` will show no diff. That avoids replacement but is a manual step — schedule a maintenance window if unsure.

alex: I tried manual attach:
```
aws elasticache modify-replication-group --replication-group-id rg-staging --parameter-group-name redis-legacy-mod --apply-immediately
```
It accepted and didn't restart nodes. After `terraform refresh` plan shows no change. Whew.

jin: :thumbsup: Good. Can you add a short note in the terraform repo about this drift and the origin? Also maybe add `prevent_destroy` lifecycle on replication_group to avoid accidental replacement.

alex: Will add a note and open a tiny PR to add `prevent_destroy = true` on the replication_group. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812

marta: Also create the parameter group resource in TF next time so we don't drift. I'll follow up and make that change.

alex: Thanks all. Lock/attach workflow saved the day. Leaving this thread in case someone else hits it.
